document.description: The project document the draft belongs to.

payload.description: The complete structured shadow to validate and store.

source.description: The draft prose the payload quotes and hashes.

AtomExpr.description: A predicate applied to a list of argument terms, e.g. `adjacent(a, b)`.

BeatKind.description: A beat's kind — a try, a fail, or an accomplishment (§7.1, §3).

oneOf.description:
An accomplishment — the beat the season's `accomplishment-earned` rule
joins over.

BeatRow.description: A beat: a try, fail, or accomplishment with a thread and a magnitude (§7.1).

line.description: The draft line the quote sits on (1-based).

outcome.description:
The try/fail typing, when the extractor carried it — sharpens the season
`accomplishment-earned` join (spec §3 reads the failure set
{yes-but, no-but, no-and} from here; `None` degrades to reading
[`kind`](Self::kind), so a payload that records only the coarse
try/fail/accomplishment signal still joins).

quote.description: The verbatim draft text this beat is drawn from.

scene.description: The scene the beat sits in.

thread.description: The thread the beat belongs to — the identity the season join runs on.

Claim.description: A factcheck atom, anchored to the draft (§7.1).

atom.description:
The atom in surface form, e.g. `holds(enfys, consent(household, door))`.
`PAY-2` parses this into a typed atom for the fact-checker. The 0.6.3
typed successor is [`Self::atom_expr`]; this string form is a registered
field-level killed form, refused from contract 1.0 and still accepted —
and still **required** — before it.

`default` is what lets a 1.0 caller send [`Self::atom_expr`] alone: a
retired field cannot also be a mandatory one. The pre-1.0 requirement is
restored verbatim on the wire by `dli_serve`'s
`serve::required_retired_field`; a payload read from disk was never
version-negotiated and is unchanged either way.

atom_expr.description:
The claim as a typed atom — the 0.6.3 typed successor to [`Self::atom`],
carried structurally instead of re-parsed at the load boundary. When
present the fact-checker uses it and [`Self::atom`] is not parsed; when
absent the surface form is parsed exactly as before.

Skipped when absent, so a payload that does not carry it — every stored
and committed payload written before 0.6.3 — serializes byte-identically.

line.description: The draft line the quote sits on (1-based).

quote.description: The verbatim draft text this claim is drawn from.

oneOf.description: A character (or the listener) learns a fact.
Possession of an object changes hands.
A character takes or heals an injury.

DeltaRow.description:
A knowledge / possession / location / injury delta the draft records (§7.1).

Deltas carry no quote and are not quote-anchored — they are the state moves
the continuity fold consumes, keyed by scene and line for provenance.

fact.description: The fact / object / place / injury moved.

line.description: The draft line the delta is drawn from (1-based).

scene.description: The scene the delta happens in.

ExtractorManifest.description:
The extractor manifest: the schema version, and the model + prompt that
produced each extracted field (§7.1).

The lexicon and banned-vocabulary rows are deterministic scans with no model
involved, so they carry no [`ExtractorRef`].

fields.description: The extractor identity for each extracted field (`beats`, `claims`, …).

ExtractorRef.description: The identity of the model and prompt that produced one extracted field (§7.1).

model.description: The model that produced the field.

prompt.description: The `sha256:` hash of the rendered extraction prompt.

FileId.description: Identifier for a source file within a compilation.

Ident.description: A named identifier. Either the bare text, whose span is synthetic, or an object carrying the text and an optional span.

span.description: A half-open byte range within a single source file.

file.description: The file this span points into.

Lexicon.description:
The deterministic lexicon scan carried in the payload (§7.1).

No model is involved: these ride along so the report is one artifact, but they
are not encodings and carry no extractor.

banned_hits.description:
Banned-vocabulary hits the deterministic scan found (empty in a clean
draft).

register_tokens.description: The count of register-true tokens the scan saw.

Magnitude.description:
A beat's dramatic magnitude — the scale the `accomplishment-earned` rule
reads (§3).

oneOf.description: A climax-class beat — requires two prior failures on its thread.

NameIntro.description:
The proper names a payload introduces (§7.1). Each is oracle-vetted or
hypothesis-carried by the naming family in `PAY-2`.

introduced.description: Names first used in this episode.

Payload.description:
The structured shadow of a drafted episode — `payload/v1` (§7.1).

The top-level keys mirror the spec's worked YAML exactly: [`meta`](Self::meta)
(source hash and extractor manifest), [`claims`](Self::claims),
[`deltas`](Self::deltas), [`scenes`](Self::scenes), [`beats`](Self::beats),
[`promises`](Self::promises), [`proof_ledgers`](Self::proof_ledgers),
[`names`](Self::names), and [`lexicon`](Self::lexicon).

beats.description: Beats: tries, fails, and accomplishments with threads and magnitudes.

claims.description: Factcheck atoms, each anchored to a draft quote and line.

deltas.description: Knowledge / possession / location / injury deltas the draft records.

lexicon.description: The deterministic lexicon and banned-vocabulary scan (no model involved).

meta.description: Source provenance and the extractor manifest.

proof_ledgers.description: Per-scene proof ledgers, replayed through the practice checker in `PAY-2`.

scenes.description: Scenes: cast, presence, location, phase observations.

PayloadMeta.description: The payload header: source provenance and the extractor manifest (§7.1).

extracted.description: The date the payload was extracted (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

extractors.description: The extractor manifest: schema version and per-field extractor identity.

source.description: The source draft this payload pins.

PromiseKind.description: The kind of promise made to the listener.

PromiseLedger.description: The promises a payload opens and closes (§7.1).

PromiseRow.description:
One promise the draft opens or closes, anchored to its opening/closing quote
(§7.1). [`kind`](Self::kind) reuses the outline schema's [`PromiseKind`] so a
payload promise and an outline promise speak the same vocabulary.

line.description: The draft line the quote sits on (1-based).

quote.description: The verbatim draft text the promise is drawn from.

ProofClose.description: A proof's conclusion: the atom it closes on and the verdict it expects (§7.1).

atom.description: The atom the casting closes on, in surface form.

ProofLedger.description: The premises, steps, and close of a shadowed proof (§7.1).

close.description: The casting's conclusion and expected verdict.

premises.description: The premises the casting rests on, in surface form.

steps.description: The proof steps, in surface form.

ProofLedgerRow.description:
A scene's proof ledger — the shadow of a diegetic proof block (§7.1).

`PAY-2` replays it through the practice checker with the scene projection
([`04-practices`](../../../../docs/spec/04-practices.md)).

scene.description: The scene the ledger belongs to.

SceneRow.description: A scene's cast, presence, location, and phase observations (§7.1).

phases.description: The phase in force for each cycle in the scene (`tide` → `slack`).

SourceRef.description: The draft a payload shadows, pinned by content hash (§7.4 staleness).

sha256.description:
The `sha256` hex of the draft content this payload shadows. A `sha256:`
prefix is tolerated on read ([`check_staleness`]).

words.description: The draft word count at extraction time.

Term.description: A term: a variable, symbol, literal, or time reference.

oneOf.description: A ground symbol naming an entity.
A reference into the time domain.

TimeRef.description: A reference to a named era or event on the timeline.

TryFailOutcome.description: A try/fail outcome, typed on the yes/no × but/and grid.

oneOf.description: Succeeds, but at a cost that complicates.
Fails, but a consolation opens a path.
